strings.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
strings.role: President of Brazil · Former trade union leader
strings.summary: Lula rose from metalworker and union leader to Brazil’s presidency, serving from 2003 to 2010 and returning in 2023. He expanded income support and antihunger policies during economic growth and strengthened Brazil’s role in Global South cooperation. Corruption investigations led to imprisonment and electoral disqualification; his convictions were later annulled over jurisdiction and judicial bias. He won reelection again in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: Rose from trade-union leadership to Brazil's presidency, advancing poverty reduction and Global South diplomacy, with broad influence on Latin American politics and international cooperation.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-01.value: Garanhuns region, Pernambuco, Brazil, in what is now Caetés
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education and training
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Lathe-operator training at Brazil’s National Industrial Training Service (SENAI)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Poverty reduction and income support
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Expanded social policies including Bolsa Família; growth and cash transfers together improved living conditions.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: From trade unionism to the presidency
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Helped found the Workers’ Party, repeatedly contested the presidency and returned after legal and electoral setbacks.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Won another presidential election
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Defeated Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff, winning a further term that had not yet begun.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Returned to the presidency
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Began his third presidential term after defeating Jair Bolsonaro in 2022.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Corruption convictions annulled
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The Supreme Court upheld annulment for lack of jurisdiction and separately found judicial bias, reopening his electoral path.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Imprisoned and barred from the election
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Corruption convictions led to imprisonment and exclusion from that year’s presidential race; the convictions were later annulled.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Won presidential reelection
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Won the runoff and continued social protection and development policies.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Launched Bolsa Família
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Consolidated cash transfers supporting low-income families, with conditions tied to schooling and health services.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Became president for the first time
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Took office after winning the 2002 election, bringing a trade union leader to the center of national power.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Elected to the constituent legislature
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Entered the Chamber of Deputies and participated in drafting the democratic constitution.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Helped found the Workers’ Party
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Joined trade unionists and social movements in forming the Workers’ Party.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Led metalworkers’ strikes
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Organized labor action in the ABC industrial region under military rule and rose to national prominence.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Completed vocational training
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Combined factory work with SENAI training as a young man and became a metalworker.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Pernambuco
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Moved to São Paulo state with his family as a child; migration and industrial work shaped his early life.
